content.rendered: Alyx is the Assistant Controller at Founders Fund. She assists with the firm’s financial reporting, tax return review, and day-to-day accounting responsibilities. Previously, Alyx worked at Deloitte Tax LLP based in San Francisco in the real estate, private equity, and venture capital markets. Additionally, Alyx spent time at Deloitte LLP in London helping foreign companies with US tax exposure. When Alyx is not crunching numbers, she is playing pickleball, reading, or cooking.

Amin is a partner at Founders Fund. He has worked on the firm’s investments across stages, including Ramp, Stripe, Ohalo, and Netic. Previously, he was an investor at General Atlantic and received his BA in Economics from Yale.

Bridget is an Associate at Founders Fund. Previously, she worked at Pantera Capital focusing on early-stage crypto investments. Bridget studied Economics (BA) and Computer Science (MS, unfinished) at Stanford.

Danielle is the Head of Legal Operations at Founders Fund. She supports the firm’s legal operations, including managing investment transactions, maintaining legal documentation and facilitating communication among internal teams, external counsel, and portfolio companies.

Prior to joining Founders Fund, Danielle worked in the office of the CEO at General Catalyst, acting as a strategic partner and building her operational understanding of the venture capital landscape. Earlier in her career Danielle worked at Samsara, a leading telematics start-up, where she gained valuable experience scaling within a high growth company.

Delian is a Partner at Founders Fund and President and Co-Founder of Varda Space Industries. Varda is manufacturing pharmaceuticals and advanced materials that can’t be made as effectively on Earth, and enabling cutting-edge microgravity research. He also co-created the Hill & Valley Forum, which brings together leaders from Washington and Silicon Valley to strengthen collaboration on technology and national security.

Denny Lai is the Senior Controller at Founders Fund. He is responsible for financial accounting, reporting and analysis for the firm’s investment partnerships as well as day-to-day finance matters. Prior to Founders Fund, Denny was an auditor at BDO, a public accounting firm, where he focused on venture capital and private equity audits.

 Denny is a native San Franciscan. He received a BA in Economics with a focus in Accounting from the University of California, Los Angeles and is a Certified Public Accountant.

Dior is the Senior Fund Accountant at Founders Fund. She began her career as an auditor at PwC in San Francisco, serving clients across asset management and private equity. Dior is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and studied Business Administration with a concentration in Accounting at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo.

Ellie Pearson is the Head of Recruiting and Operations at Founders Fund. Previously, she was a founding member of the sales team at Square (Block). After the IPO, Ellie went on to specialize in executive search where she worked with early & growth stage founders to build out their go-to-market leadership teams.Her love for team building began in college where she was the team captain of the 2013 NCAA undefeated National Championship women’s basketball team.

Elly is Chief of Staff to Trae Stephens at Founders Fund. She joins from Tilia, where she led channel partnerships and account management. Prior to that, she worked in business development at Meta with a focus on blockchain. After graduating from Stanford, she started her career as executive assistant to Peter Thiel.

Erin Gleason Lane is the Chief Communications Officer at Founders Fund. She drives communications strategy and media relations for the firm and serves as an advisor to portfolio companies. Before joining Founders Fund, Erin was a member of the executive team at The Hatch Agency. Prior to that, she oversaw public relations as one of the earliest employees at Foursquare. Erin began her career at Google in New York, working on internal and external communications for the engineering executive team. Erin received a BA from Stanford University.

Joey is a Partner at Founders Fund. Joey previously served as Co-CIO at Pantera Capital, one of the largest blockchain-focused investment firms, which he joined in 2017. There, he invested in the first institutional rounds of companies like Starkware, Arbitrum, and Alchemy. He is co-founder of the Forecast Foundation, which contributes to the development of Augur, and a co-founder of Eco, a simple balance that lets you spend, send, save and make money at the same time. Prior to Pantera, Joey built a sound-based point-of-sale payment system. 

Joey started programming in Applesoft BASIC when in middle school after his dad bought him an Apple II GS on eBay. He studied CS in college because he enjoys being able to translate his ideas into code. He started angel investing in 2016 and co-started a top-ranked AngelList Syndicate. Joey is a Thiel Fellow and an Edmund Hillary Fellow.

John is a Partner at Founders Fund. He has worked on investments including Scale AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Cognition, Rippling, Figma, Newfront Insurance, Flock Safety, Loop Logistics, and Specter. He received his BS in Computer Science from Stanford University, where he was Editor-in-Chief of the Stanford Review.

​​Josh is Director of Tax at Founders Fund. He focuses on partnership taxation, financial reporting, and investor relations.

Prior to joining Founders Fund, Josh worked at Deloitte advising on tax issues and coordinating tax compliance for clients in the alternative investment industry. He studied accounting and finance at Cal Poly in San Luis Obispo where he received both his BS in Business Administration and MS in Taxation with honors.

Koren Gilbai is an Associate at Founders Fund. Previously, Koren served in Israel’s IDF cybersecurity units and performed vulnerability research at Google. Koren holds a BS with distinction in Computer Science from Stanford

Lauren is a Partner and COO at Founders Fund. She works closely with the investment team and leads all non-investment activities, which include running internal operations and overseeing the firm’s legal, finance and branding teams. Lauren works with the partnership on key strategic decisions and investments and also leads fundraising and management of the firm’s limited partner relationships.

Prior to Founders Fund, Lauren spent four years at Clarium Capital Management LLC, a global macro hedge fund. She began her financial career at Citigroup Investment Bank, where she was an analyst in the technology group. Lauren graduated with honors in Economics from Stanford University.

Matias is a partner focused on growth and international companies. Since joining Founders Fund in 2018, he has backed companies including SpaceX, Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Figma, Wave, Persona, and Scale. He serves as a board director or observer at Trade Republic, Enter, Arq, and Kavak.

Previously, Matias invested at Insight and CapitalG, partnering with CrowdStrike, UiPath, Qualtrics, and Looker. He also operated at Wallapop, a consumer marketplace later acquired by Naver. He holds a BS in Finance and Information Systems from NYU Stern.

Matias is from Buenos Aires and now based in Miami, after a decade in San Francisco, New York, Barcelona, and Shanghai.

Michael is the Chief Marketing Officer at Founders Fund. He is also the founder of Pirate Wires, a media company focused on the intersection of technology, politics, and culture. He runs creative programming for Founders Fund, including the Anatomy of Next podcast as well as Symposium (F50), the firm’s annual summit, and Hereticon, a conference for thoughtcrime.

Mike is the Creative Director at Founders Fund, where his aim is to produce enduring brand experiences through thoughtful, if often unconventional design. Over the past 15 years, he has created all of Founders Fund’s visual index, from its distinctive logo and floating-heads to the widely shared Opening Notes montage and an extensive apparel catalog. He was Art Director and Set Designer for Hereticon and Hereticon: Apocalypse Ball, as well as Co-creator and Co-producer of Mafia.

Outside of Founders Fund, Mike advises We Landed, a creative agency focused on building innovative companies and technologies.
Napoleon is a Partner at Founders Fund and focuses on growth. He holds an MBA from Stanford and a BS from the University of Colorado.

Natasha is the Head of Brand Operations at Founders Fund. She oversees event logistics, production, and provides project support for the Brand Team. Previously, Natasha spent 12 years at Twilio, where she played a pivotal role in enhancing employee and customer experiences, helping the company grow from 60 to over 9,000 employees. Originally from Colorado, she’d always rather be outside.

Neil is the General Counsel at Founders Fund. He oversees the legal affairs of the firm, including investment structuring and negotiation, portfolio company management, and fund formation and governance.

Prior to joining Founders Fund, Neil was Vice President and Associate General Counsel at Thiel Capital, where he provided strategic and operational support for Peter Thiel’s investment initiatives and entrepreneurial endeavors. Neil began his legal career at Sidley Austin, an international law firm, where his practice included mergers and acquisitions, securities work, and general corporate governance of public and private companies. Neil received his JD from Harvard Law School and BA degrees in Economics and Sociology from Duke University.

Neil is the Chief Financial Officer at Founders Fund. He leads the Finance team and is responsible for the financial reporting of the firm’s investment funds as well as the day-to-day finance and management company matters.

Prior to joining Founders Fund, Neil was the Controller at VantagePoint Capital Partners, a leading global investor in energy, innovation and efficiency. He was previously the Controller at 3i, an international investor focused on private equity, infrastructure and debt management, and prior to that, the Accounting Manager at investment banking firm Merriman Curhan Ford. Neil began his career at Ernst & Young LLP, where he served as an Audit Manager in the financial services group. He is a qualified chartered accountant and received his Bachelor’s degree with honors from the University of Johannesburg in South Africa.

Peter Thiel is an entrepreneur and investor. He cofounded PayPal, led it as CEO, and took it public; he made the first outside investment in Facebook; and he cofounded Palantir Technologies, where he serves as chairman. He has provided early funding for LinkedIn, Yelp, and dozens of startups, many run by former colleagues who have been dubbed the “PayPal Mafia.” He is a partner at Founders Fund, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm that has funded companies including SpaceX and Airbnb. He started the Thiel Fellowship, which funds young entrepreneurs, and he leads the Thiel Foundation, which works to advance technological progress and long-term thinking. He is also the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future.

Robert is on the investment team at Founders Fund. Previously, he conducted theoretical physics research at the University of Munich, ETH Zurich, and UC Berkeley. Robert holds both a BS and MS in Physics from the University of Munich.

Ryan is a Partner at Founders Fund. Previously, she was a VP at OpenAI leading AI safety work, a Product Director at Meta leading election integrity & social issue teams, and a VP at Palantir where she led development of Gotham, an analysis platform deployed across military, intelligence, and civil agencies in democracies around the world. She holds a BA in political science from Northwestern University, graduating summa cum laude. At university, she was a champion policy debater, where she and her partner were the #1 ranked team in the US. Ryan was also awarded the top individual speaker award at the college national championship in 2012 – the fourth woman since 1946.
Sam is the Head of IT at Founders Fund. Previously, he was the Head of IT at Greenoaks Capital and K1 Investment Management. He holds a BS in Electrical Engineering from NYU.

Scott is a Partner at Founders Fund. He works with mission-driven founders rearchitecting industries. Scott supports Synthego, Collective Health, Modern Animal and over a dozen more engineering-driven startups across biotech, crypto, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing and transportation.

Prior to Founders Fund, Scott was an early employee at SpaceX, where he helped develop the original Falcon propulsion systems and multiple Dragon subsystems. After SpaceX, Scott worked at Bain & Company with its private equity clients and co-founded a consumer internet company built on the Facebook Connect API.

Scott earned Bachelor and Master degrees in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from Cornell in under four years and received his MBA from Stanford University, where he was co-president of the Entrepreneurs Club and voted “most likely to drop out” by his peers.

Sean is a Partner at Founders Fund. Prior to joining Founders Fund, Sean was CFO of Solugen, where he led the finance, strategy, and operations functions, and supported the company’s scale up from initial pilot to its first commercial facility. Prior to Solugen, Sean held various investment and operating roles across Asia and the US at Silver Lake, Google, Vy Capital, and SoftBank. Sean earned a BS in International Economics from Georgetown University, and is an avid long distance runner and biker.

Spencer Devereaux is the Director of Finance at Founders Fund. He spearheads portfolio company valuations, playing a crucial role in maintaining accurate financial reporting and analysis and supporting investor relations efforts. 

Spencer began his career at Deloitte, where he earned his CPA certification and specialized in financial technology audits for private and public companies, including IPOs. He has over six years of industry experience and holds a Bachelor’s degree in accounting from Santa Clara University, where he graduated with honors.

Driven by a passion for continuous learning, Spencer spends his free time expanding his knowledge of emerging investment trends, with a particular personal interest in cryptocurrencies. This curiosity fuels his ability to navigate the ever-evolving landscape of finance and offer innovative perspectives to his colleagues.

Trae is a Partner at Founders Fund. He is also Co-founder and Executive Chairman of Anduril Industries, a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems.

Previously, Trae was an early employee at Palantir Technologies, where he led teams focused on growth in the intelligence/defense space as well as international expansion, helping large organizations solve their hardest data analysis problems. He was also an integral part of the product team, leading the design and strategy for new product offerings. While at Palantir, Trae also served as an adjunct faculty member at Georgetown University.

Prior to Palantir, Trae worked as a computational linguist building enterprise solutions to Arabic/Persian name matching and data enrichment within the United States Intelligence community. He began his career working in the office of then Congressman Rob Portman and in the Political Affairs Office at the Embassy of Afghanistan in Washington, D.C. immediately following the installation of Hamid Karzai’s transitional government. Trae graduated from the School of Foreign Service at Georgetown University.
